WHAT WORKS, WHAT IS MISSING, WHAT BREAKS
CALIBRATE FIRST

Calibrate once so your takes land on the beat. Headphones on, it takes about 20 seconds.

MANUAL
QUICK START

Put on headphones, then:

  1. Open SETTINGS (grid icon) and tap CALIBRATE once, so your takes land on the beat.
  2. Set the tempo (BPM) and turn LOOP on.
  3. Tap RECORD. After the count-in, sing.
  4. Tap RECORD again to stop. The loop closes on a full bar and starts playing.
  5. Tap RECORD again to add the next layer on top.
RECORD SCREEN

BPM sets the tempo for click, count-in and loop length. CLICK switches the metronome: ON (sound), VISUAL (silent, for recording without headphones) or OFF. With ON or VISUAL the display shows the beat: SONAR rings in the middle of the meter, four beat bars on top and the corners kicking out. During the count-in four rings close in on the center and burst on the one. GAIN is the input level. COUNT-IN gives one bar of clicks before recording, or none.

BARS sets a fixed loop length: FREE, 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars. With a fixed length the recording stops by itself, so you can focus on singing. It only works with LOOP on.

The arc is your input meter. The six rings inside show the layers of the loop: a box lights up where a layer has sound and flashes while it plays. The status line always says what happens next.

LOOPING AND OVERDUB

With LOOP on and BARS on FREE, a recording ends on a full bar. Stop in the first half of a bar and it cuts back to the bar line, stop in the second half and it finishes the bar. With LOOP off you record a ONE-SHOT of any length.

While a loop is selected, every RECORD adds exactly one round on top (overdub) and stops by itself. RECORD during an overdub cancels it.

  • One loop holds up to 6 layers.
  • The loop point is seamless, there is no click where the loop starts again.
  • To start a fresh loop, tap NEW LOOP in TAKES.
  • IMPORT in TAKES loads an audio file as a take, for testing without singing. A BPM in the file name (like _120_) sets the tempo, and if the length fits whole bars it becomes a loop.
SING OVER A TRACK
  1. In Audiotool, bounce the part of your track you want to sing over. It lands in your library.
  2. Open SETTINGS (the grid top right), go to LOOP, tap LIBRARY and log in if asked. REMOVE takes the loop out again.
  3. MY SAMPLES lists your own loops, newest first. SEARCH looks through the public library. The BPM key limits results to your tempo.
  4. Tap the play symbol to preview, USE to load it. DREX-MB takes over its tempo and shows READY: OVER BACKING.
  5. Tap RECORD. Your layers are exactly as long as the backing loop.

The backing loop plays 3 dB lower, does not count as a layer and never goes through the FX. In EDIT the box B mutes it. It is never exported, so your vocals drop straight back onto the same spot in your track.

TAKES

Every recording is one take, no matter how many layers. Saved takes and their settings stay in your browser.

  • Names are automatic: SINGLE LOOP 120 03, MULTI LOOP 120 03 or ONESHOT 03. Rename in EDIT or EXPORT.
  • Tap a row to select it, its mini wave to open EDIT, DEL to delete it.
  • A new take is unsaved until you tap SAVE, on the main screen or in TAKES. Only saved takes stay in TAKES. If you move on without saving, DREX-MB asks first. An unsaved take left from last time is offered again on the next start.
  • Nothing is selected at start, so your first RECORD always starts a new take.
EDIT

EDIT works on one layer at a time. Boxes 1 to 6 pick the layer, B mutes the backing loop.

Timing: draw a region over the wave and drag it to fix a late or early phrase. AUTO suggests regions, SNAP or FREE sets the grid, COPY duplicates, DEL silences, RESET undoes all. 1X, 2X and 4X zoom in. One-shots also get trim handles.

VOL, S (solo), M (mute), PAN, WID (stereo width) and DEL LAYER.

PITCH: moves the whole take up or down in semitones (-12 to +12): all layers, all effects and the background loop together, the tempo stays. It is worked out in the background, until then you hear the last version. Tap the value to go back to 0.

NR (noise reduction, 0 to 100): in pauses noise is removed by RNNoise (an open source neural network from Xiph.Org) down to -24 dB at 100; while you sing only a calm, steady reduction of at most 6 dB runs, so the voice itself stays untouched. DE-ESS finds your S sounds and tames only the sharp peaks. Both are worked out when you let go, it takes a moment (CLEANING).

EQ: 8 bands from 80 Hz to 10 kHz plus low and high cut. Drag the points. FLAT, WARM, THIN, BRIGHT and PHONE are quick starting points.

FX

After EDIT everything is about the sum: all layers together go through the FX chain. The backing loop never does.

Chain: VOCODER, SNADPAD and MULTI. Tap a device to show it, the light shows if it is on. The arrows move the shown device left or right in the chain. Tap the tab of the page you are on (ROBO, VOCODER, SNADPAD, MULTI) to turn it on or off, the line in the tab lights up when it is on. FX settings are saved with the take.

SNADPAD MB: the original SNADPAD engine. Tap and drag on the scope to play. Double tap sets a point, tap a point to hold it, double tap it to remove it, drag to move it. RUN travels the points, GLIDE smooths the way, RATE sets the speed. REC records your finger on the pad for exactly one round of LEN (1, 2 or 4 bars) and then stops by itself, the move loops right away. Press REC again for another round, it only replaces where you play. Every pass adds to the move: where you play, the new movement replaces the old one, the rest stays. UNDO and REDO step back and forth, LOOP pauses or plays the move, LEN sets its length (1, 2 or 4 bars), DRIFT lets it wander a little every round. The arrows on the ring switch the set. CATCH and FLUSH work in the set CRUMBS. Knobs: drag up for more, double tap to reset.

ROBO: the robot voice, first tab in the FX bar, switches on as soon as you open it. Every sixteenth note plays exactly one note, so the robot steps cleanly instead of wobbling. Inside the circle your take runs three times as rings, cut into steps (eighth notes, the numbers mark the bars): outside HIGH, middle MID, inside LOW. Every step starts in the middle. Drag a step outward or inward and it jumps into that ring, keep dragging along the ring to move a whole passage. Tap a ring to drop a step right there. The robot is one voice, hard and monophonic like Daft Punk: the energy comes from jumping, for example one word an octave down. Your melody sits inside the ring of its step, the playhead runs along. HIGH, MID and LOW below are the tuning wheels of the three rings (HIGH 0 to +24, MID -12 to +12, LOW -24 to 0 semitones, start one octave up, unchanged, one octave down) and land on notes of the scale. TONE picks SAW, SQUARE or SOFT, GLIDE lets notes slide, CLEAR puts all steps back in the middle. Your real voice is gone completely, even S, T and SH are rebuilt from noise in the color of your voice. While ROBO works it keeps playing the last robot result (the very first time the track is silent). MIX brings your real voice back underneath if you want it (starts at 0). The key is found by itself, tap a note on the outer note ring to set it yourself, SCALE switches MAJOR, MINOR and CHROM. ROBO works in the background (ROBO WORKING) once per setting, moving steps is instant. It is part of the export. Below the circle: UNDO and REDO step back and forth through every effect change of this take (all tabs, steps, knobs, on and off). AS LOOP turns everything you hear right now (all layers with all effects, plus a background loop) into a new background loop, so you can sing on top of it. Your take stays as it is.

VOCODER: your voice shapes a carrier. The top row picks it: CHORD plays a synth chord, DRONE a deep single tone, NOISE gives a whisper, SAMPLE picks any sound from your Audiotool library. Tap a note on the ring to set the key. MAJ, MIN and PWR set the chord and the scale. FOLLOW makes CHORD or DRONE follow your singing in that key, without it they hold the key note. OCT switches between LOW and MID. CLARITY brings out consonants, VOICE blends your own voice back in.

MULTI: MODULATION, PULSE, CHOP, SHAPE, DELAY and REVERB. DELAY and REVERB have their own engines, MOD runs on the real STOMPINSKI engine. Tap a button to pick the effect (green frame), it lies in the circle and its knobs show below. Tap it again to switch it on or off (light on the button). Playing the circle switches the picked effect on. Hold a button and drag left or right to change the order, the ring shows the chain. HOLD is on by default: the effect stays where you leave it. With HOLD off the effect only sounds while your finger is on the circle, like a Kaoss Pad: tap a word into the delay and the echo rings out after you let go. HOLD on keeps the effect and the point where you left it. ROUTE switches the picked effect between SEND (your voice stays dry, the effect is added, MIX is the send level) and INSERT (the whole voice goes through it, MIX blends dry and effect). DELAY and REVERB start as SEND. The circle plays: MOD rate and depth, SHAPE curve and drive, REVERB size and level. DELAY is a clock: once around is one bar, the 1 sits at the top. Double tap the circle to place an echo (up to 8), drag it to move it, double tap on an echo removes it, further out is louder. GRID snaps to 1/16, 1/16 T, 1/32 or FREE. The delay works like a tape echo with several heads: FEEDBACK sends all echoes back onto the tape, so a few points grow into a rolling rhythm. TAPE adds wow, flutter and saturation that grows with every repeat, later repeats get softer and smear. DUCK pushes the echoes down while you sing and lets them bloom in the gaps. WIDTH spreads the echoes left and right and lets the repeats cross over. LOW CUT, HIGH CUT and RESO shape the echoes, every repeat gets thinner or darker. Echoes dragged into the outer ring (EDGE) get dirty. REVERB SOUND switches between VOCAL (filtered send, the reverb ducks while you sing and blooms in the gaps) and CLASSIC. PRE sets how late the reverb starts and stays put. PUMP pushes the reverb away on every beat and lets it swell back. EDGE: the right edge of the circle is the experimental zone (marked). In the middle everything stays clean, towards the edge REVERB gets scratched by a fuzz, DELAY saturates and starts to whistle, MOD turns metallic, The EDGE knob sets how strong the zone gets, 0 switches it off. The knobs below hold all other settings of the picked effect, the arrows page through them. MOD has four modes (CHORUS, FLANGER, PHASER, VIBE), DELAY switches between SYNC (note values) and FREE (milliseconds), TONE darkens the echoes, REVERB has ROOM (short and close), DARK HALL (long, dark, floating) and PLATE (bright and dense, the vocal classic). Everything else is set for vocals. PULSE makes the voice pulse in time. The circle works like a clock: around it sit note values from 1/4 to 1/64 (straight and triplets), the distance from the centre is how deep it pulses, the centre does nothing. DEPTH sets the maximum depth, SHAPE goes from SOFT edges to PUNCH, GATE sets how long each pulse stays open (short blips to long), PHASE turns the pulse into left and right movement at 180 DEG. Page 2 makes it sound like a synth: FILTER makes every pulse pluck a low pass filter like a synth bass (snaps open, then closes within the pulse), RESO makes it whistle, S&H gives every pulse its own random filter height, SWING pushes every second pulse later (up to a hard 75 percent swing). 1/64 gets so fast that it turns into a buzzing tone. The outer ring breathes with the pulse, left half for the left side, right half for the right side. REC, RUN and HOLD work like on the other effects. CHOP cuts your take into up to 16 syllables as soon as you open it, each with its own colour, numbered in the order you sang them. They sit in the inner ring: tap one to pick it (you hear it). The outer ring is one bar with 16 steps: tap a step to put the picked syllable there, tap it again to clear it, double tap to play it backwards. Drag a step outwards or inwards to change its pitch, drag along the ring to make it longer. Tap the centre for a suggestion, then change it step by step. CLEAR empties the pattern, UNDO and REDO step through your pattern changes. LEN makes the pattern 1, 2 or 4 bars long: new bars start as a copy, the small bar buttons at the top of the centre pick which bar the ring shows for editing, the playing bar lights up and the ring follows it while playing (it stays put for 4 seconds after you pick a bar or edit). STEP shows the pitch of the last step you touched and lets you turn it (on a computer the mouse wheel over a step does the same), TRANSPOSE moves everything up or down, GATE goes from short and choppy to letting each syllable ring, SWING pushes every second step later. Page 2 only shapes the suggestion: DENSITY how many steps, RANGE how far the melody jumps, EDGE octave jumps. CHOP always uses the main take, not its layers. If the VOCODER sits before MULTI in the chain and is on, CHOP cuts the vocoded voice (it takes a moment to update after vocoder changes); if it sits after MULTI, the chops go into the vocoder. SHAPE is a guitar fuzz: left to right the gain, bottom to top the feedback, from the middle on it starts to whistle and sing like a guitar in front of the amp and rings out a little after you stop singing. TONE sets the top end.

MULTI REC AND RUN: works like the SNADPAD. REC records your finger in the circle for exactly one round of LEN (1, 2 or 4 bars) and then stops by itself, the move loops right away. Press REC again for another round, it only replaces where you play. A ring around the circle shows how far the round is. LEN is set for each effect on its own. UNDO and REDO step back and forth, LOOP pauses or plays the move, LEN sets its length. Every effect keeps its own move, a red dot on the ring shows it. Double tap the circle to set up to 8 points, double tap a point to remove it, drag it to move it. RUN travels the points with playback, RATE sets how long each point lasts, GLIDE slides between them. Touch the circle any time to take over. Export plays all moves and runs along.

Export includes the whole chain in your order. On SNADPAD it includes what you recorded with REC, held points and RUN. Free playing without REC is live only.

EXPORT

What you hear is what you export. The backing loop is never included.

  1. Select a take and open EXPORT.
  2. Log in with Audiotool.
  3. Check the NAME.
  4. Pick MIX (all layers), LAYER n (one layer) or ALL LAYERS (one file each).
  5. Tap EXPORT TO LIBRARY. Loops are uploaded with their BPM.

FINALIZER: vocal mastering on the sum. RAW keeps it neutral. CLEAN is open and transparent: balance, glue and level. WARM adds tube color and body, smooths harsh mids. BRIGHT is modern pop: tight lows, presence, lots of air, parallel compression and a little width. LOUD is dense and loud for rap and club tracks. CLEAN and WARM land around -14 LUFS, BRIGHT around -12, LOUD around -9. The limiter also catches peaks between samples (-1 dBTP), so nothing clips after export. Tap PLAY to hear it, you can switch while it plays. The choice is saved with the take.

DOWNLOAD WAV saves the same file to your device. Uploads are hidden by default in Audiotool.

SETTINGS

CALIBRATE: headphones on, four high clicks count in, then clap along to 8 clicks. Do this once per device and when you change headphones.

LEVEL: every take is brought up so its loudest moment sits at -6 dB. Nothing else is changed automatically, cleaning is up to you in EDIT.

FINGERPRINTS: shows a glowing print wherever you touch, gone after a moment. A light tap leaves a fingertip, a held or dragged finger a full print. OFF switches it off.

SET LEVEL: tap it and sing for four seconds as loud as in the song. GAIN is set so your peaks land at -6 dB. Double tap GAIN on the main screen does the same. GAIN goes up to +24 dB for quiet microphones.

CLICK PITCH: tunes the metronome to a note, so you can sing in key.

THEME: switches between dark and bright.

TOUR: a guided tour through every button, in ten chapters. Each step points at the real button and waits until you have tried it. SKIP opens the chapter list, done chapters are marked.

FEEDBACK: send a message straight to the developer: what works, what is missing, what breaks. Name and email are optional, add an email if you want an answer.

HOME SCREEN

iPhone in Safari: Share in the bar below, then Add to Home Screen. iPhone in Chrome: Share in the address bar top right, then Add to Home Screen. Android: menu (three dots), then Add to home screen. DREX-MB then starts full screen like an app. The icon version keeps its own takes.
